title: Open restriction preserves formal kernels before abelianness
statement: Let $X$ be Noetherian, let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, and let $U\subseteq X$ be an open subscheme which is Noetherian. For every morphism $\alpha:F\to G$ in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], the actual termwise restriction functor of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-restriction-objects] preserves the kernel diagram $(\alpha,0)$. This is preservation of categorical formal kernels, not levelwise kernels, and assumes no abelian structure.

proof.text: Obtain c, the shifted-image system S with inclusion j, its quotient system K, inclusion iota and transition-zero bound from the existing construction theorem. Prove j_m alpha_m=0 by naturality and the epi image factorization; then cancel the quotient projection and the quotient isomorphism to prove iota alpha=0.

The proved private formalMono_of_kernel_transition_zero helper in CoherentFormalModuleKernel uses epi source transitions to turn the transition-zero bound into monicity of iota. Apply the existing factorization theorem and construct the limiting KernelFork on X.

Use the actual restriction functor on formal objects. The ordinary module restriction functor preserves sheaf kernels, epimorphisms and monomorphisms. Its kernel comparison and the restricted epi-mono factorization identify each restricted S_m, with its inclusion, as the image of the later restricted kernel in the restricted F_m.

The coherent levels of F and G are quasi-coherent; closure under kernels and cokernels and the image presentation give quasi-coherence of every S_m. Reuse the proved private powerQuotientIso and powerQuotientIso_pi helpers in FormalSystemsPullback. Transport their tensor-pullback comparison along the left-adjoint isomorphism with ordinary restriction. Its projection equation follows from quotientMap_pi and naturality of that isomorphism. Compose with the restricted e_n and map the original transition and inclusion equations, obtaining exactly the hypotheses of the factorization theorem on U.

The ordinary sheaf-kernel comparison writes the new kernel inclusion as the inverse comparison followed by the restriction of the original kernel inclusion. Compose with the restricted transition and map the original zero equation. The same transition-zero monicity helper proves monicity of the restricted formal inclusion. Apply coherentFormalModule_kernel_factorization on U to the transported presentation; existence and monicity give a limiting mapped kernel fork.

Use KernelFork.isLimitMapConeEquiv to pass from the mapped fork to the mapped cone. Mathlib preservesLimit_of_preserves_limit_cone transports this one limiting cone to every limiting cone for parallelPair alpha zero.
